messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Region sa-east1 — several customer VPN sessions reporting egress blackholed to on-prem. Impacting customer 'Acme Retail' (vpn-945). Auto-triage suggests BGP withdrawal on DX peer. Please acknowledge and join.

oncall-mike: on it. paging in. I can see alerts for vpn-945 and increased 5xx on embedding API for that tenant.

network-alia: I’m pulling BGP state from sa-east1 DX/VRF now.

oncall-mike: confirmation: customer reports 40% of requests to embeddings time out, others succeed. Likely asymmetric egress. Is this a complete outage?

se-john-cust: Customer-side: they see TCP SYNs hitting our edge then nothing back. Some flows succeed via their second DC but primary DC gets no return.

network-alia: BGP summary from our sa-east1 DX router:
```
Router# show bgp ipv4 unicast summary | include vpn-945
Neighbor 10.200.3.2    4 05:12:43  ESTABLISHED  0/0/0    0
Neighbor 10.200.4.2    0 00:00:02  Idle (Admin)  0/0/0  
```
We have the peer to the customer's primary eBGP neighbor stuck in Idle after a flapping event. Routes from that peer are not in RIB.

ops-raj: any config pushes recently to that DX edge?

infra-bot: deploybot: no recent infra deploys targeting sa-east1-dx-edge in last 24h.

oncall-mike: ok, immediate mitigation options: 1) force failover to customer's secondary VPN/peer via our routing policy 2) announce a more-specific route we own to steer return path 3) request customer to reset their eBGP session. Which is fastest?

network-alia: fastest is to enable routing policy override for vpn-945 to prefer the eu-west1 egress. That's a soft change on our side and avoids asking customer for action. I'll prepare the policy.

oncall-mike: go for it. mark it as temporary and document TTL.

network-alia: applying policy now:
```json
{
  "route_policy": "prefer-eu-failover",
  "match": "prefix == 10.45.0.0/16 and tag == vpn-945",
  "action": "set next-hop = eu-west1-nat; local-pref = 200"
}
```
Policy applied to outbound egress for tenant prefix 10.45.0.0/16 — traffic should steer via eu-west1 within 30s.

oncall-mike: monitoring... dashboards show drop in 5xx for Acme embedding API from 68% -> 12% within a minute. Good.

se-john-cust: we see traffic returning now, thank you. Their app latency is back to normal for most flows. They will keep monitoring.

network-alia: parallel action: I’ve opened ticket with cloud provider for the DX peer flapping. Possible MTU mismatch or upstream maintenance. Ticket #CLOUD-9921 created, assigned to network ops.

ops-raj: can we capture tcpdump on the sa-east1 edge to prove whether RSTs or drops were happening? I want pcap for postmortem.

oncall-mike: yes, go ahead. Raj, coordinate with Alia for exact interface.

ops-raj: running tcpdump now for 5 minutes on vrf-vpn-945 egress interface. Saving to s3:/incidents/1729234567/pcap.

infra-bot: automation: scheduled a config rollback checkpoint before policy change (checkpoint id cp-1729234567).

network-alia: follow-up diagnostic: show ip route for customer prefix showed no route via peer-10.200.4.2; after policy change routes prefer eu-west1-nexthop.

oncall-mike: customer impact now mitigated by failover. Next steps: 1) wait for cloud provider fix on DX peer 2) if fixed, revert the emergency policy and test graceful failback 3) collect pcaps and BGP logs for postmortem.

se-john-cust: can you notify customer about temporary reroute and expected next steps? They asked for ETA.

oncall-mike: I'll send a short update: "We've routed egress traffic for your sa-east1 prefix via our eu-west1 failover while we work with the cloud provider to restore the primary DX peer. No config change required on your side. We will notify you when we revert."

se-john-cust: thanks — they acknowledged and appreciate the quick mitigation.

network-alia: provider update: their maint console shows a flapping SES interface due to hardware firmware bug; they’re doing a forced restart now. ETA 18-25 mins. Ticket updated.

oncall-mike: ok. set a timer for 30m for re-eval. If provider fixes and peer re-establishes, we will test BGP failback by prepending and lowering local-pref then remove emergency policy.

ops-raj: pcap captured. I see SYNs hitting our edge, no SYN-ACK from our internal path while peer was down. After policy switch, SYN-ACKs resumed via eu-west1. Pcap link: https://s3.redwood/incidents/1729234567/pcap.gz

eng-sam: curious: should we add an automatic routing fallback when routes from DX peers withdraw more than X minutes? Might reduce manual ops here. Filing follow-up ticket for Optimize: RB-135 (auto-regional-failover).

network-alia: agreed. short term: I will add a runbook step to cutover to failover region and document the exact CLI commands we used. Long term: RB-135 to propose automated policy activation based on BGP withdrawal alarms.

oncall-mike: handoff: I need to step out in 20m. @oncall-mike -> @ops-raj will take primary for monitoring and customer comms after 20m. Raj, please watch for ticket CLOUD-9921 status and re-evaluate failback when peer is up.

ops-raj: acknowledged. I’ll watch for provider events and confirm re-establishment. I’ll also coordinate a brief smoke test with the customer before we revert.

network-alia: provider reports peer ESTABLISHED at 1729240100, routes are being re-advertised. I see routes back in RIB.

ops-raj: starting planned failback test: temporarily lower local-pref and remove prefer-eu policy for vpn-945 for 5 min test window.

ops-raj: removing policy now. Monitoring.

se-john-cust: we see traffic switching back without errors. No increased 5xx.

ops-raj: good. leaving standard policies in place. closing mitigation. Will open postmortem with timeline, pcaps, BGP dumps, and action items (auto-failover runbook + RB-135).

network-alia: action items:
- upload all BGP dumps and pcaps to incident folder (done)
- draft postmortem (assigned to Alia)
- implement runbook step and add to oncall playbook (Raj)
- prioritize RB-135 in next Optimize sprint (Sam)

oncall-mike: thanks team. Logging the incident as sev3 for now (customer impact but mitigated). I’ll annotate timeline and hand to PM for customer-facing postmortem.

se-john-cust: thanks again. They’re happy with the communication.

incident-bot: Incident closed for oncall-mike handoff. Final status: mitigated, primary peer restored, routes healthy.

network-alia: starting postmortem doc now: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/1729234567-sa-east1-vpn-egress-blackhole.md

ops-raj: throwing a quick reminder: add the exact CLI commands used to the runbook so new oncall can do this in <10 min next time.

eng-sam: filed RB-135 and linked incident.

oncall-mike: great work. :thumbsup:
